outcome: Correlation of skinfold thickness, anthropometric measurements, and estimated body fat percentage with mode of delivery
cohort: 41 pregnant women who were overweight or obese with singleton pregnancies
finding: Greater weight, waist circumference, Huston-Presley body fat percentage, and specific skinfold thicknesses in the third trimester were associated with an increased risk of cesarean delivery in overweight and obese women.
mod_finding: The study found an association between greater weight, waist circumference, Huston-Presley body fat percentage, triceps skinfold thickness, biceps skinfold thickness, sum of skinfold sites, and cesarean delivery.
